source_priority: Owner-requested plausible horse anatomy and stronger conical muzzle, using the approved imagined side study for unseen side form
Original black and white Lichess 300px sprites for set character and overhead comparison
Selected black candidate 2 enlargement for secondary detail interpretation

reference_camera.basis: Initial whole-set elevation from rook estimate; still an interpretation

geometry.method: One continuous skull/cheek/chin/muzzle envelope joined to neck; tapering cross-sections continue down to a small rounded cone end; inset upper-lateral almond eyes and small nostril recesses; laid-back ears and inward-filled arched mane; established turned pedestal

observations: Previous 196,806-triangle model was rejected after rotation despite its high silhouette overlap; its separate jaw volume read as a hanging bag.

Four corrective anatomy studies removed the separate jaw, moved the eye to the upper skull, restored laid-back ears from the approved concept, joined the mane to the neck, and progressively tapered the muzzle tip.
True level profile, front, three-quarter, side, opposite and reference-camera renders were visually inspected.
Front and Side viewer presets now correspond to muzzle-facing and horse-profile views.
Original silhouette IoU is 0.92495 and mean boundary discrepancy is 3.14 original pixels. These record the overhead difference; they are not an anatomy quality score.
limitations: The generated side study is an owner-approved interpretation, not recovered geometry. The 54-degree camera and unseen bilateral depth remain inferred.
Small carved features and surface transitions remain artistic approximations; original overhead silhouette agreement decreased with the authorized anatomy correction.
Mane, ears, eyes and pedestal remain separate closed components intersecting the continuous head-neck skin. They are not fused for manufacturing.
Neutral clay lighting differs from the reference wood; wood grain and materials have not been reconstructed.
Browser rendering was not exercised; controls, horse front/side presets and exact saved-camera projection were checked with the Node VM harness.
